entries.reason: Selects the rule file and the Conduit plugins.
The bucket objects are written to.
Kafka Connect trims the list and splits it on commas with surrounding whitespace; written the same way.
A Conduit pipeline reads its source with one reader; Kafka Connect ran several tasks. Parallel readers arrive with partition claims (v0.24).
entries.fix: For sinks, raise sdk.batch.size on the destination if throughput falls short.

entries.reason: Kafka Connect rotates a file after flush.size records; Conduit writes one object per batch, so sdk.batch.size bounds the records per object instead.
Conduit's json format writes one OpenCDC-shaped object per line (Operation, Position, Payload, Key, Metadata); Kafka Connect's JsonFormat writes the bare record value.
entries.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if consumers read the bare-value JSON lines, or accept the difference with --accept-gaps.

entries.reason: The Hive schema generator names the object schema; Conduit has no schema generator.
entries.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if a Hive metastore reads the schema, or accept the difference with --accept-gaps.

entries.reason: Conduit has no schema compatibility mode.
entries.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if a schema registry or Hive metastore enforces compatibility.

entries.reason: Kafka Connect writes objects under topics/<topic>/partition=<n>/; Conduit writes them under <prefix>/<UnixNano>.<ext>, so the object layout differs.
entries.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if consumers read the partitioned object keys, or accept the difference with --accept-gaps.

notes.reason: Conduit writes one object per batch as <prefix>/<UnixNano>.<ext>; the Kafka Connect S3 sink names and lays out objects by its partitioner, and its JsonFormat writes the bare record value where Conduit's json format writes one OpenCDC-shaped object per line. Consumers of the exact object keys or line shape break.
notes.fix: Keep this connector on Kafka Connect if consumers read the object keys or the bare-value JSON lines, or accept the difference with --accept-gaps.

notes.reason: Object names are not deterministic, so a batch that is retried after a failure or a restart is written again as a new object. A reader can see a record twice, never zero times; Kafka Connect's deterministic naming gives exactly-once object keys.
notes.fix: None needed; consumers should tolerate duplicate objects.

notes.reason: Kafka Connect reads a sink's topics in the consumer group connect-<name>, and the Kafka source defaults to a new random group. groupID is set to connect-sink-s3-00, so the pipeline resumes from the offsets the Kafka Connect sink committed to that group.

Kafka Connect's consumer defaults auto.offset.reset to earliest, and the Kafka source defaults to the end of each partition. readFromBeginning is set to true: a partition the group has no committed offset for is read from its first record, as Kafka Connect does, and a partition with a committed offset resumes from it.

The pipeline's Kafka source reads in the consumer group connect-sink-s3-00, the group the Kafka Connect sink commits its offsets to, and resumes from them. While the Kafka Connect connector is still running, both consumers are in the group and Kafka splits the partitions between them, so neither sees every record. Records the sink processed after its last committed offset are read again, so they can reach the destination twice.
notes.fix: Stop the Kafka Connect connector (PUT /connectors/<name>/stop, or delete it; pausing keeps its group membership) and wait until kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group connect-sink-s3-00 lists no members, then start the pipeline.

notes.reason: The builtin:kafka source requires servers, and no key of the Kafka Connect config sets it; the pipeline references ${KC_SINK_S3_00_SOURCE_SERVERS} instead.
notes.fix: Set KC_SINK_S3_00_SOURCE_SERVERS in the environment (see secrets.env.template), or pass the worker file with --worker if it holds bootstrap.servers.

notes.reason: The builtin:s3 destination requires format, and no key of the Kafka Connect config sets it; the pipeline references ${KC_SINK_S3_00_DESTINATION_FORMAT} instead.
notes.fix: Set KC_SINK_S3_00_DESTINATION_FORMAT in the environment (see secrets.env.template).

notes.reason: Neither the connector nor a worker file sets key.converter, so the format Kafka Connect used is unknown.
notes.fix: Pass the worker properties with --worker, or set key.converter on the connector, then re-run.

notes.reason: Neither the connector nor a worker file sets value.converter, so the format Kafka Connect used is unknown.
notes.fix: Pass the worker properties with --worker, or set value.converter on the connector, then re-run.

notes.reason: Kafka Connect does not retry a failed operation by default (errors.retry.timeout=0). Conduit restarts a failed pipeline through pipeline recovery, so a transient failure that stopped the connector may not stop the pipeline.
Kafka Connect's default header converter types header values; Conduit carries headers as metadata strings.
